title: Tech Note: Logging Off an Inactive User
author: Kent Wilbur
featured_technology: Custom processes and DELAY PROCESS/PAUSE PROCESS/RESUME PROCESS

historical_commentary.text: This note presents a hand-built, blended polling/event-driven technique for auto-logging off idle 4D Server users to free concurrent-usage licenses and improve security, plus a controlled-shutdown pattern using custom processes and OUTSIDE CALL; the core business need (session timeout, freeing licenses, graceful save-before-quit) is timeless, but the specific low-level implementation (manual process scheduling with DELAY PROCESS/ON EVENT CALL, licensing model tied to concurrent connections) reflects a pre-modern 4D architecture that has been significantly modernized.
related_updates: 4D has since added built-in idle/session timeout and user management capabilities in later versions, reducing the need for this fully hand-rolled polling/event technique
4D's licensing model and client/server architecture have evolved considerably since the mid-1990s 4D Server 3.x/6.0 era
Events and Methods terminology (replacing Phases and Procedures) arrived in 4D V6 (1997), the same year this note's underlying language concepts predate
